decision: Ratify or strengthen the completeness policy for persistent empty closed-history responses and repository-count drift?
whyItMatters: Repeated empty 200 responses are not independently verified closed-history absence. Conservative full-page refusal can also stall a closed-history walk.
evidence: The inherited census cross-checks open_issues_count, refuses false-empty and unverified-empty open listings, and confirms open walks. LiveGh verifies open totals exactly.

Closed listings have no independent total: the inherited watcher accepts a history that is empty on every attempt, and refuses a full-page terminal boundary without a count. Those limits are preserved, not claimed fixed.
The current mission runs mocked tests only, including false-empty, linked-empty, missing-link and exact-multiple cases. No live census or closure dry run has been used to resolve the question.
recommended: Review a trustworthy independent closed-count source and its completeness contract before relaxing any refusal. Keep unknown coverage visible.
alternative: Retain the current conservative boundaries and explicitly accept their residual false-empty risk and stalls.
unblocks: Completeness-policy ruling; never authorization to close issues.
